goalDescription: Die lernende Person kann Informationsasymmetrien, öffentliche Güter und Monopole als Marktversagen erklären.
reviewerModel: Codex; exact serving model identifier not exposed
aspectRatioDecision: Close native 16:9 landscape; no exception needed. Existing format not mechanically normalized.

actualInspection.fachlichePruefung: Three examples match the current goal: a closed backpack with uncertain buyer and seller thought cutaway for information asymmetry; one flood-warning signal heard by several neighbors for a non-rival, non-excludable warning in this model; and one visible bicycle supplier with a barrier blocking a new shop for monopoly entry problems. No image claims that every shared physical good is public or every lone supplier is inefficient.
actualInspection.phone: At 360 px all three headings and the uncertain buyer, shared warning, existing shop and closed entry barrier remain recognizable. Warning wave/bell and forbidden new-shop icon carry meaning without the small sign text.
actualInspection.desktop: At 680 px the thought bubble originates by the seller while the buyer has a separate question, and the public warning is clearly a signal rather than rival bottled water. The entry barrier is explicit.
actualInspection.actorPerspective: The buyer looks toward the closed backpack; no hidden product information is falsely shown as a page they can read. Neighbors face the public signal; shoppers and entry sign face the market scene appropriately.
actualInspection.style: Friendly approachable comic raster, clear broad colors, large conceptual objects; no photorealistic or sterile technical restyling.

interpretationLimits: This is a conceptual introduction. It does not establish current legal market boundaries, quantify welfare loss or prove a particular seller is abusive.
goalTextStatus: Current German competence unchanged in the E2 bilingual candidate; this image review does not attest the positive-evidence profile or bilingual description gate.
